# Explain index

`cloudseed explain` knows **306 pages**. Each one is available the same way everywhere: `cloudseed explain <query>` in the terminal (`--json` for data), the **?** buttons and the Explain panel in the [web console](../guides/web-console.md), and `cloudseed_explain` / `cloudseed://explain/<query>` over [MCP](../guides/mcp.md). See the [explain guide](../guides/explain.md).

!!! info "Generated from the code"
    This page is generated by `scripts/gen-docs.py` from the explain index (`cloudseed/explain.py`), so it always matches the CLI you install (this build: cloudseed 0.1.0).

|---|---|
| Features | 26 |
| Targets | 4 |

## Features

| Name | What it explains | Command |
|---|---|---|
| `operations` | Shared health, deployment, policy, upgrade and recovery workflows with explicit evidence and approval gates. | `cloudseed explain operations` |
| `overview` | How cloudseed is built: a stdlib Python CLI, Terraform stacks per target, Ansible for hosts, a Helm catalog and agent skills. | `cloudseed explain overview` |
| `network` | One non-overlapping address space per environment: public and private subnets, NAT egress, flow logs, deny-by-default firewalls. | `cloudseed explain network` |
| `bastion` | A single hardened SSH jump host, reachable only from your IP, with key-only auth, an encrypted disk and Ansible hardening. | `cloudseed explain bastion` |
| `security-baseline` | Account- and project-wide guard rails, each managed by one environment: CloudTrail, GuardDuty, audit logs, Defender, encryption defaults. | `cloudseed explain security-baseline` |
| `state` | Terraform state per environment: a versioned, encrypted bucket or storage account bootstrapped first, or local files. | `cloudseed explain state` |
| `kubernetes` | Managed clusters (EKS / GKE / AKS, private endpoint by default) or RKE2 / kubeadm on VMware, one kubeconfig per environment. | `cloudseed explain kubernetes` |
| `platform` | A curated Helm / kustomize catalog in groups, installed in dependency order with values per target and private load balancers. | `cloudseed explain platform` |
| `vpn` | An OpenVPN server with per-user profiles, or a Tailscale subnet router, giving your machine a route into the private network. | `cloudseed explain vpn` |
| `vmware` | Local VMs on VMware Fusion Pro 13+ / Workstation Pro 17+ through cloudseed's own Terraform provider, on a host-only network. | `cloudseed explain vmware` |
| `provisioning` | After apply, the repository is copied to the hosts over SSH and Ansible hardens them and installs the tools. | `cloudseed explain provisioning` |
| `finops` | Cost estimates from the inventory, actual cloud bills and Kubernetes cost allocation with OpenCost, saved as reports. | `cloudseed explain finops` |
| `managed-data` | Databricks and Snowflake through their official CLIs, with a private connection profile per environment. | `cloudseed explain managed-data` |
| `agentic` | An optional agent (built-in, Claude Code, Codex, Gemini or Grok) that drives cloudseed while credentials are kept away from it. | `cloudseed explain agentic` |
| `reconcile` | Terraform runs survive 'already exists': only objects provably this environment's are imported, and the new plan is approved again. | `cloudseed explain reconcile` |
| `mcp` | cloudseed as an MCP server: one tool per feature plus resources and prompts, over stdio or local HTTP with a token. | `cloudseed explain mcp` |
| `prereqs` | Cloud resources platform items need (Velero buckets, Karpenter roles, identities) come from the environment's own Terraform stack. | `cloudseed explain prereqs` |
| `fips` | fips\_mode=true builds the whole environment for FIPS 140: endpoints, images, hosts, algorithms and a gated platform catalog. | `cloudseed explain fips` |
| `chaos` | Chaos Mesh experiments against a canary or your Deployment, with an availability hypothesis and a PASS / FAIL report. | `cloudseed explain chaos` |
| `dr` | Velero backups to storage the stack creates, restores, schedules, and automated drills that measure the recovery time. | `cloudseed explain dr` |
| `scan` | Security scanners and a separate local Well-Architected assessment, with saved reports and explicit verdicts. | `cloudseed explain scan` |
| `architecture` | Assess saved configuration and evidence against provider guidance; missing evidence remains unknown and no cloud resources are changed. | `cloudseed explain architecture` |
| `undo` | A journal of the last fifteen actions per environment (and fifteen global ones, at most five of one kind) with their inverse: cs undo reverts the newest. | `cloudseed explain undo` |
| `ui` | A local, token-protected web console where every cloudseed capability is a form and a button, and a "?" explains each one. | `cloudseed explain ui` |
| `audit` | Every command writes an audit line and a redacted log; inventory.json tracks resources and changes; troubleshoot reads them. | `cloudseed explain audit` |
| `dependencies` | Tools installed locally (Homebrew or verified releases), in a container image, or as one self-contained bundle. | `cloudseed explain dependencies` |

## Targets

| Name | What it explains | Command |
|---|---|---|

| `azure` | What cs setup azure builds on Azure: a VNet with NSGs and a NAT gateway, a hardened bastion, Log Analytics, optional AKS, VPN, FIPS and Defender. | `cloudseed explain azure` |
| `vmware` | What cs setup vmware builds on your machine: VMs on a host-only network, host and architecture detection, guest OS choices, every variable and output. | `cloudseed explain target vmware` |

## Platform groups

| Name | What it explains | Command |
|---|---|---|
| `basek8s` | Cluster management: metrics, certs, Gateway API + Envoy Gateway (private LB), GitOps, observability (Prometheus, Loki), OTel, secrets. | `cloudseed explain basek8s` |
| `scaling` | Autoscaling: KEDA, VPA + Goldilocks (+ metrics-server), cluster-autoscaler / Karpenter (cloud). | `cloudseed explain scaling` |
| `data` | Data platform: MinIO, Postgres operator, Kafka, Spark, Trino, StarRocks, Polaris, Airflow, ClickHouse. | `cloudseed explain data` |
| `ai` | AI/ML: Ray, Kubeflow trainer/pipelines, KServe, JupyterHub, MLflow, vLLM, GPU operator, Ollama. | `cloudseed explain ai` |
| `agentic` | Agentic: kagent, kmcp, agentgateway, Qdrant, Langfuse, LiteLLM, Open WebUI. | `cloudseed explain group agentic` |
| `finops` | FinOps: OpenCost (+ Prometheus), kube-green, Kubecost; pairs with `cs finops` for cloud bills and estimates. | `cloudseed explain group finops` |

| `chaos` | Chaos engineering: Chaos Mesh (+ LitmusChaos extra); `cs chaos run` executes automated experiments with a PASS/FAIL report. | `cloudseed explain group chaos` |

## Setup variables

Every stack variable and setup input has its own page: `cloudseed explain variable <cloud> <name>` (or `cloudseed explain <cloud> <name>`). The full tables live on the target pages:

| Target | Variables | Reference |
|---|---|---|
| AWS | 39 | [aws](aws.md#stack-variables) |
| Google Cloud | 36 | [gcp](gcp.md#stack-variables) |
| Azure | 29 | [azure](azure.md#stack-variables) |
| VMware (local) | 28 | [vmware](vmware.md#stack-variables) |
